---
title: "Accessibility"
---

The theme treats accessibility as a non-negotiable requirement, not a
nice-to-have. Every accent surface, every link, every callout, every
focus cue has been audited against WCAG 2.2 AA at minimum.

## Two-channel link cue

Prose links carry **three** distinguishing cues, not one:

- **Colour** — Starbuck blue (light) / Starbuck light (dark)
- **Underline** — 2 px Starbuck-tinted, 0.18em underline offset
- **Weight** — 500 (medium) rather than the body's 400

The combination of colour-plus-underline satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 (do
not rely on colour alone). On monochrome renderers (e-paper, fax
printouts, high-contrast OS modes), the underline and weight cues
still distinguish links from body text.

The cue is scoped to `main`, `article`, `.content`, and
`.quarto-document-content` so navbar / sidebar / TOC / footer /
anchor / citation links keep their own treatments and don't drown the
page in underlines.

## Focus indicator

`:focus-visible` carries a **body-colour** outline + a **Starbuck**
box-shadow glow.

```scss
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid $body-color;
  outline-offset: 2px;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px rgba($link-color, 0.35);
}
```

A pure-blue outline alone would not pass WCAG 1.4.11 contrast
against the warm-paper background (~3:1, below the 3:1 cap-floor for
non-text contrast against an adjacent colour). The body-colour
outline carries the primary contrast; the Starbuck glow rides as the
brand cue.

## Callout palette — all five colours hold AA

| Callout | Light role | Light hex | Light contrast against `$log-50` | Dark role | Dark hex | Dark contrast against `$log-950` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | Starbuck | `#0082B1` | 4.58:1 | Starbuck dark | `#A6DFFF` | 15.2:1 |
| `tip` | Tashtego | `#177C55` | 5.18:1 | Tashtego dark | `#82C4A2` | 10.4:1 |
| `warning` | Stubb | `#CA6435` | 4.61:1 | Stubb dark | `#FFD9BB` | 16.1:1 |
| `caution` | Pip | `#6A4A00` | 8.84:1 | Pip dark | `#DEC577` | 12.7:1 |
| `important` | Ahab (danger) | `#A83732` | 7.46:1 | Danger dark | `#F47A6E` | 8.92:1 |

The colour-coded left rule is reinforced by a tinted header with the
same crew colour and a Bootstrap icon — so the callout type is
distinguishable to colour-blind readers (the rule + icon + label
text carry the information together).

## Reduced motion

Both formats honour `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

- **HTML** disables theme smooth-scroll. Bootstrap 5's own
  `$enable-reduced-motion: true` covers component-level animations
  (modals, dropdowns, …).
- **Reveal** clamps `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` to
  `0.01ms` on every `.reveal *` descendant. Reveal's slide transition
  is already set to `none` by default in the extension, but downstream
  callouts and fragment animations can still animate without this
  clamp.

## Print

The HTML format ships a print stylesheet that:

- Hides navbar / sidebar / TOC / footer / repo actions / search
- Prints `(href)` after every external link so readers on paper can
  follow them
- Strips code-block surface fills (saves toner)
- Prevents page breaks inside headings, figures, and tables

External link URLs are excluded for `localhost`, citations, and the
`.no-underline` class.

## Skip nav

Quarto's built-in skip-link sits at the top of every HTML page
(`<a class="skip-link" href="#quarto-content">Skip to content</a>`).
The theme styles the focused state with the same body-colour
outline + Starbuck glow as the rest of the focus indicators.

## Self-hosted fonts (GDPR + offline)

Both Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono are
shipped as base64-inlined woff2 inside `_pequod-fonts.scss`. No
network requests fire at page-load time; the page renders the
institutional typography even with the user offline or with a
strict Content-Security-Policy `font-src 'self'` rule.

The Typst format ships static-weight TTFs under
`_extensions/pequod/fonts/` for the same reason — Typst loads them
through `font-paths: [fonts]` (relative to the extension dir).
